title: Sifuna's US tour moves to Maryland and DC after packed Allentown town hall
key_points: The Allentown, Pennsylvania town hall on Sunday was filled to capacity, Mwakilishi and K24 reported.
Sifuna opened the movement's first overseas office in Hackettstown, New Jersey.
Today (Nov 24) he has a policy meeting and a luncheon with Maryland elected officials; Wednesday ends with a town hall.
Next stops: Dallas and Houston, then Seattle and California, ending December 7.
content:
WASHINGTON, DC — Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna's tour of the United States has reached Maryland and the Washington DC area, after a busy first weekend in New Jersey and Pennsylvania.

Sifuna leads the Linda Mwananchi Movement (LMM) and wants to run for president in Kenya's August 2027 election. His trip runs from November 21 to December 7, according to Mwakilishi, a news site for Kenyans in the US.

What happened at the weekend

In our Sunday story, we promised to report what happened at the Allentown town hall. Here it is.

  • New Jersey: supporters met him at Newark airport with songs, dances and banners. He opened the movement's first office outside Kenya, in Hackettstown, New Jersey. Mwakilishi said the office will run volunteer work, voter outreach and fundraising on the East Coast.
  • Pennsylvania: on Sunday, November 22, he went to a morning service at Grace Community Church in Allentown. In the afternoon, he spoke at a town hall at The Palace Center. Mwakilishi said the hall was full, with Kenyans from Pennsylvania, New York and New Jersey. K24 Digital said a video Sifuna shared showed every seat taken.

At the town hall, Sifuna answered critics who had doubted his support in the region. He talked about governance, economic accountability and the constitution, Mwakilishi reported.

This week in Maryland and DC

  • Monday, Nov 23: business community dinner in Maryland.
  • Today, Tuesday, Nov 24: an East Africa politics and policy meeting, then a luncheon with Afri Thrive and Maryland elected officials.
  • Wednesday, Nov 25: a brunch with women from the DC area, a talk with the 6.25 Movement and Gen Z Movement, and an evening town hall.

The rest of the tour

  • Texas: Thanksgiving dinner with families in Dallas on November 27; women's meeting and town hall in Houston on November 29.
  • Washington State: December 3–4, church service in Federal Way and a gala dinner in Renton.
  • California: December 5, town hall in San Francisco and a gala in Oakland; December 7, closing dinner with Kenyan professionals in Silicon Valley.

Dates and venues can change, so check with local organisers before you travel.

Why it matters

Kenyans abroad send home billions of shillings every year. But very few vote: fewer than 600 Kenyans living in the US were registered to vote in 2022, Mwakilishi reported. Analysts say tours like this one matter mostly for raising campaign money and shaping debate at home.

Back in Kenya, the opposition is asking the electoral commission to allow electronic voting for Kenyans abroad. That could change how much the diaspora vote counts in the future.

Other leaders, including Rigathi Gachagua and David Maraga, have made similar trips to the US. The Nation noted that these tours include a large fundraising part.
